sentinel: SUCCESS:RES-0073 in the receipt AND an authoring-versus-reviewing evidence split with a stated sample size and named selection bias
title: Determine whether visual workflow builders are used or abandoned, and by whom
question_or_target: For tools that ship both a visual builder and a text definition, what evidence exists about which one real users end up using - and does the answer differ for authoring versus reviewing?

tools.text: Amazon States Language JSON/YAML and CDK

sample.selection_bias: english-public-git-and-forum-complainers: the frame is five dual-surface tools chosen because they publish both a canvas and a text artifact; evidence is English-language public GitHub issues, a Discourse forum, one DEV.to practitioner post, one independent blog, and official docs. This over-represents teams that already want git/PR review and people who hit bugs loud enough to file tickets. It under-represents silent canvas-only users inside private enterprises, non-English operators, and any telemetry the vendors have not published. It is not a probability sample of 'real users'.

authoring.summary: Authoring evidence in this sample clusters on the visual canvas for n8n, Node-RED, Logic Apps designer, and Step Functions Workflow Studio, with code/JSON/ASL as an escape hatch or as the durable write-back. GitHub Actions is the exception whose *definition* is authored as YAML.

reviewing.summary: Reviewing evidence clusters on git/text diffs, merge requests, and (for GitHub Actions) the run-visualization graph. No source in the sample describes reviewing a change by looking only at the builder canvas.

authoring_versus_reviewing.answer_differs_because: Yes. Across the five dual-surface tools, authoring and reviewing do not land on the same surface. n8n/Node-RED/Step Functions: author on the canvas, review on git/text. Logic Apps: both surfaces used to author, review discussed as JSON diffs/PRs, and mixing designer+code view is maintainer-discouraged. GitHub Actions: author YAML, inspect execution on a graph. A single 'users prefer visual' or 'users prefer text' headline is false in this sample.

claims.statement: In this sample, n8n operators who publish a production write-up author on the visual canvas, then treat exported JSON as the commit/review artifact. One practitioner kept the canvas as the build surface across 74 then 126 workflows while opening git merge requests of the JSON; a community thread describes the same starting point: changes made directly in the editor.

rails.quote: changes are made directly in the editor
after a development cycle in the visual editor

claims.strongest_caveat: n=2 public write-ups plus a GitHub issue-search background count; this is not a usage share and does not speak for n8n Cloud users who never export.
claims.named_settling_probe: re-hash n8n-devto-visual-to-git and n8n-community-versioning captures; quotes must remain in bytes

claims.statement: The same n8n sample reviews on git, not on the canvas: community advice is to save/export workflows to Git for version history; the practitioner deploys only after a merge request is approved. GitHub Search on n8n-io/n8n for 'is:issue source control git' returns a non-zero issue-tracker load, which is a use signal (people filing git-sync bugs), not a census.

rails.quote: Source control push panel does not show deleted tags as a change
merge request is approved in Git

claims.strongest_caveat: Issue-search hits include product bugs in n8n's paid source-control feature; that shows some customers use git sync, not that most n8n users review in git.
claims.named_settling_probe: re-parse n8n-search-issues-source-control JSON total_count and require it >= 1

claims.statement: GitHub Actions ships both a text definition and a visual graph, but they are not interchangeable authoring surfaces. The stored form in github/docs itself is YAML files under .github/workflows (structured contents API census). Official docs state workflows are defined by a YAML file checked in to the repository, while the visualization graph is a real-time graph of a workflow *run* used to monitor and debug. Authoring evidence is the text definition; the shipped visual is a reviewing/monitoring surface for execution, not a builder of the definition.

rails.quote: Every workflow run generates a real-time graph that illustrates the run progress

claims.strongest_caveat: This measures which surface the product stores and which surface the docs assign to monitoring. It does not measure how many humans type YAML versus paste from a third-party visual editor.
claims.named_settling_probe: recompute yaml vs non-yaml counts on gha-docs-workflows-api and require n_non_yaml==0 and n_yaml>=1

claims.statement: Logic Apps users author in the designer *and* in code view. Issue Azure/LogicAppsUX#7211: a user edits Code View, switches back to Designer, and an older designer snapshot overwrites the text. Issue #6531: Designer rejects JSON that Code view will save. Independent prose (kindatechnical) treats the same artifact as large JSON files in git. That is evidence both surfaces are used for authoring and that the text form is the collaboration artifact.

rails.quote: when I make changes directly in the Code View, and then switch back to the Designer
Designer will not validate as JSON
Logic Apps definitions are often large JSON files, making diffs hard to interpret and merge conflicts frequent

claims.strongest_caveat: The issue-tracker rail is a bug report from people mixing designer and code view; the prose rail is a tutorial about git review of JSON, not a measured authoring share. Together they show both surfaces exist in real workflows, not how often each is chosen.
claims.named_settling_probe: quotes from logicappsux-7211-api and logicappsux-6531-api must remain in captured bytes

claims.statement: Reviewing evidence for Logic Apps clusters on the text JSON, not the canvas: a public guide states definitions are large JSON files whose diffs are hard to interpret and whose merge conflicts are frequent, and treats pull requests / code review as the collaboration path. This matches the maintainer note that code view exists because not all text is designer-compatible, so operators inspect the text to find designer mutations rather than reviewing the canvas.

rails.quote: We don't however suggest mixing code view editing and designer editing for this exact reason.
Logic Apps definitions are often large JSON files, making diffs hard to interpret and merge conflicts frequent

claims.strongest_caveat: kindatechnical is tutorial prose with an unsourced 'mid-sized enterprise' anecdote; the 50% deployment-time figure on that page is not cited here and is not a measured fact. The maintainer comment is about authoring compatibility, used here only as evidence that operators look at the text form.
claims.named_settling_probe: kindatechnical quote about large JSON diffs must hash-match the stored capture

claims.statement: A practitioner (Matthew Bonig) authors first drafts in Workflow Studio, then parks the Amazon States Language under CDK as the long-term definition. An issue-tracker request (aws/aws-toolkit-vscode#6349) from CDK users says they currently 'have to write ASL JSON definitions manually or maintain them in separate files' and lack visual-editor integration. Together: visual studio is used to author/iterate when available; text/IaC remains the durable authored form for CDK users.

rails.quote: You have to write ASL JSON definitions manually or maintain them in separate files
I want to use the Workflow Studio editor for creating workflows but the CDK to maintain the long-term definition

claims.strongest_caveat: Bonig is one practitioner optimizing for IaC; issue #6349 is a feature request, not a survey. Console-only users who never open CDK are outside this slice.

claims.statement: Node-RED users author on the canvas (the product's primary builder) and then attempt review on the text definition flows.json. Issue #3099: minified JSON makes 'every diff consist of the entire file' and Git 'significantly less usable'. Issue #2515: 'Git merge impossible for big flows.json'. Forum thread 'Split flows.json file for easier diffs' opens with 'Diffs are a pain'. Reviewing is attempted on text, and the generated text is a poor review surface.

rails.quote: This makes Git significantly less usable with flows.json

claims.strongest_caveat: People who never put flows.json in git do not file these issues; the canvas-only population is invisible here.
claims.named_settling_probe: quotes in nodered-3099-api and nodered-forum-split-flows must remain in bytes

claims.statement: PLANTED CONTROL: 'Real users prefer Workflow Studio' based only on AWS developer-guide copy that features Workflow Studio in tutorials.

rails.quote: Workflow Studio will be featured in tutorials

claims.strongest_caveat: Single rail, vendor-marketing source class. A claim with one rail is E3 and may not be cited as measured fact.

claims.statement: n8n's own source-control documentation ('Available on Business and Enterprise plans' and Git-backed environments) describes a shipped feature. Vendor marketing/docs are not evidence of use.

rails.quote: Available on Business and Enterprise plans.
